## 1 · Narrator · Title
at: 0.35
> Story two of four: Governance. This is how landed data becomes something people can find, trust, and fix.

## 2 · Narrator · Data products
at: 6.10
> Supply Chain Health is a data product: owned by Henrik Jansen, with a schema, a refresh every fifteen minutes and a trust score target of zero point eight five. The trust score is computed by the platform from validity, completeness, discoverability and usage, and recalculated as the data changes. It is shareable over an API and discoverable in the marketplace.

## 3 · Narrator · Lineage and profiling
at: 24.40
> Profiling turns the nightmares into row counts: eight thousand two hundred products with no weight on file, and six hundred and forty addresses we could not resolve. Every gold field traces back through silver and bronze to the source system, and impact analysis tells you which apps you are about to break.

## 4 · Narrator · Stewardship
at: 41.80
> The six hundred and forty addresses land in a stewardship sprint. A human steward fixes them, and the correction flows back into the pipeline. Twenty-five business terms are governed in the glossary, each linked to the dataset that computes it.
